bBC-nXj3Ng4.summary: 3Blue1Brown explains the math and mechanics behind Bitcoin visually: ledgers, digital signatures, proof of work and the blockchain, building up a decentralized payment system from first principles.
bBC-nXj3Ng4.why: The go-to recommended video for newcomers wanting a clear, visual explanation of how Bitcoin and blockchains work.

bKGhvKyjgLY.summary: R. Stanley Williams of HP Labs gives a keynote on the memristor, covering the physics, crossbar computation, and potential for memory and new computer architectures.
bKGhvKyjgLY.why: Recommended for years as the best technical introduction to memristors from the person who found the physical device.

bmSAYlu0NcY.summary: John Ousterhout, Stanford professor and creator of Tcl, presents the ideas of his book A Philosophy of Software Design in a Talks at Google session. He covers managing complexity, deep modules and interfaces, and what he teaches in his Stanford software design course.
bmSAYlu0NcY.why: HN treats it as the standard one-hour teaser for the book and recommends it for its deep-modules thinking before buying or reading the book.

bglWCuCMSWc.summary: Not Just Bikes explains how North American speed limits are set and why posted limits matter far less than street design. It argues that drivers follow the road's cues, so safe speeds have to be built into the street.
bglWCuCMSWc.why: Recommended again and again in traffic-safety threads as an eye-opener on road design versus posted limits and driver behavior.

biYciU1uiUw.summary: Dan Olson of Folding Ideas investigates the Mikkelsen Twins and the ghostwritten-audiobook passive-income course industry, even playing along with the scheme. It is a long video essay on get-rich-quick publishing grifts.
biYciU1uiUw.why: HN links it whenever threads cover book spam, AI-written ebooks or passive-income hustle culture.

bpAi70WWBlw.summary: A one-hour 2019 KOMO News documentary hosted by Eric Johnson on Seattle's homelessness and drug crisis, with interviews and looks at proposed solutions including a drug court program in Rhode Island. It argues addiction and mental illness are at the core of the problem.
bpAi70WWBlw.why: HN commenters cite it in homelessness threads about San Francisco and Seattle as an eye-opening, widely viewed argument for treatment-first policy, though some see it as pro-law-enforcement framing.

bHIhgxav9LY.summary: Veritasium argues that electric energy is carried by fields around the wires rather than by electrons moving through them, using a thought experiment with a large circuit.
bHIhgxav9LY.why: Often recommended as an eye-opening field-based explanation of electricity, though it was also controversial and criticized as pedantic.

bSkpMdDe4g4.summary: Matt Godbolt's CppCon 2017 talk shows what modern compilers do with your C++ code, using Compiler Explorer to inspect generated assembly. It covers surprising optimizations and how the tool works.
bSkpMdDe4g4.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining, mind-blowing look at compiler cleverness from a great speaker.

bJczLlwp-d8.summary: The first class of Timothy Snyder's Yale course on the making of modern Ukraine. It introduces the course and asks what it means for a nation to exist in light of the Russian invasion.
bJczLlwp-d8.why: Strongly recommended as an accessible, well-taught history of Ukraine and a counter to propaganda narratives.

bSfe5M_zG2s.summary: K Lars Lohn's PyCon 2016 keynote weaves together music theory, programming, biking road trips and fractals. It is a personal, wide-ranging talk rather than a Python how-to.
bSfe5M_zG2s.why: Commenters call it a mind-blowing, beautiful talk and cite it among their favorite tech talks.

bpQFCcSI0pU.summary: A 2020 video by laowhy86 arguing that the coronavirus did not originate outside China, pointing to evidence about the Wuhan institute and a possible patient zero. It cites sources in the description.
bpQFCcSI0pU.why: Frequently posted in early COVID origin and lab-leak threads as a compelling early case, though other commenters cite rebuttals and note it is speculative.

bRCNenhcvpw.summary: Bill Hammack of engineerguy uses slow motion video to show how the IBM Selectric typewriter works. He focuses on its fully mechanical digital-to-analog converter, which turns key presses into rotation of the type ball.
bRCNenhcvpw.why: HN commenters recommend it whenever the Selectric comes up, as a short, excellent explanation of its internals.

bRcu-ysocX4.summary: Archaeologist Eric Cline lectures on the Late Bronze Age collapse around 1177 BC, when interconnected Mediterranean empires fell in rapid succession. He discusses the Sea Peoples and the combined causes of the collapse.
bRcu-ysocX4.why: Recommended as an informative and funny hour that serves as a good substitute for his book.

bkQJdaGGVM8.summary: A short conference talk from !!Con 2017 in which Kevin Chen explains the HDR imaging algorithm from a foundational paper, framing it as a system of linear equations, and implements it in a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet. No prior image processing knowledge is needed.
bkQJdaGGVM8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a fun, short talk that shows how HDR photography actually works through an absurdly playful implementation.

bnKIVX968PQ.summary: Not Just Bikes explains how small pockets of shops and restaurants inside residential Dutch neighbourhoods create liveliness and help reduce traffic. It argues this kind of mixed-use design has been illegal in most of the US and Canada for a century because of zoning, and should be brought back.
bnKIVX968PQ.why: HN commenters link it in zoning, housing and car-dependency threads as an accessible explanation of how single-use zoning and parking rules shape cities.

bY2FlayomlE.summary: Khalil Estell's CppCon 2024 talk argues C++ exceptions can reduce binary size in firmware. He digs into how exceptions work and how to shrink their code footprint on embedded platforms.
bY2FlayomlE.why: Pointed to as the in-depth talk on exception mechanics and code size for embedded C++.

bbyr7jZOllI.summary: Kirk Sorensen's Google Tech Talk on thorium molten-salt reactors (LFTR). He covers why the technology was shelved after early development and argues that now is the right time to revisit it.
bbyr7jZOllI.why: Recommended as the go-to pitch for liquid fluoride thorium reactors whenever nuclear power comes up.

bx3KuE7UjGA.summary: Andrew Tanenbaum's FOSDEM 2010 talk on MINIX 3, a microkernel OS built for high reliability and security. It shows how the system detects and recovers from device driver crashes, and addresses microkernel performance concerns.
bx3KuE7UjGA.why: HN points to it as an accessible explanation of microkernel isolation and fault-tolerant design, and as Tanenbaum's answer to performance objections.

bAxRYrpbnuA.summary: Not Just Bikes shows how traffic calming is built into streets across the Netherlands, from city centres to villages. Street design naturally slows cars and makes roads safer.
bAxRYrpbnuA.why: HN commenters point to it in road safety and pedestrian death threads as the practical alternative to US road design.

b-7dMVcVWgc.summary: A documentary from Swan Bitcoin exploring Bitcoin's relationship with energy, featuring Lyn Alden and others, and arguing that mining is a net positive for the environment and not wasteful.
b-7dMVcVWgc.why: Bitcoin advocates on HN cite it to rebut energy-consumption and waste criticisms, though it is an advocacy piece from a Bitcoin company.

bC-8y2R6IxI.summary: Noodle explores how retro pixel art was designed for CRT displays and why games look different on LCDs, with input from pixel artists and CRT researchers.
bC-8y2R6IxI.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining deep dive on CRT versus LCD rendering of retro games and the case for CRT shaders.

bEXefdbQDjw.summary: The Thought Emporium grows living rat neurons on an electrode array and tries to train them to play Doom. It is part of a series on biological computing.
bEXefdbQDjw.why: Cited whenever biocomputing or neurons-on-chip come up, as an accessible example of how such a system can be built.

bJ5ppf0po3k.summary: A maker builds a talking banana that reads YouTube and Twitch comments aloud on stream, then fights viewers who abuse it with profanity. He ends up building a pronunciation-based filter to catch bad words.
bJ5ppf0po3k.why: HN shares it as a funny, technical story about phonetic profanity filtering, relevant to Soundex and content moderation threads.

bNfAAQUQ_54.summary: A podcast episode of Arrested DevOps with Andrew Clay Shafer and Bryan Cantrill, featuring Cantrill's rant on integrity in companies and technology.
bNfAAQUQ_54.why: HN recommends Cantrill's integrity rant when discussing corporate ethics and companies that act on principles.

bOf4EMN6-XA.summary: An eight-minute excerpt of a 1983 video featuring Seymour Papert, creator of Logo, on children learning programming and abstract ideas through embodied play. It shows kids acting out the Logo turtle.
bOf4EMN6-XA.why: Recommended to anyone unfamiliar with Papert as a glimpse of his vision for computers in education.

bY7aRJE-oOY.summary: Sid Meier's GDC 2010 keynote on how players perceive probability in games, including how Civilization's odds were adjusted because players misjudged them.
bY7aRJE-oOY.why: HN points to it as the best talk on how people misunderstand probabilities and how designers handle that.

bZQun8Y4L2A.summary: Andrej Karpathy walks through how GPT assistants are trained, from tokenization and pretraining to supervised finetuning and RLHF, and gives practical prompting strategies and a view of the tooling ecosystem.
bZQun8Y4L2A.why: Recommended as the clearest overview of how LLM assistants are built and how to use them well.

baxtyeFVn3w.summary: Aditya Siram argues that functional programming has much to learn from Smalltalk's interactivity, using Pharo and Squeak to show live, visual, explorable programming environments.
baxtyeFVn3w.why: HN recommends it as an accessible demonstration of what Smalltalk environments offer and a reference for advanced IDE ideas.

bmsV1TuESrc.summary: A nine-minute Stewart Lee stand-up routine about political correctness and the claim that it has gone mad. It is dry, layered British comedy that takes the complaint apart.
bmsV1TuESrc.why: HN commenters offer it as a sharp, funny answer to 'PC gone mad' and anti-woke arguments in discussions of language policy.

bxe2T-V8XRs.summary: The first of a short series by Welch Labs on building a complete neural network in Python. It introduces the data and the architecture of a simple network before later parts cover forward propagation, gradient descent, and backpropagation.
bxe2T-V8XRs.why: HN commenters point beginners to this series as one of the clearest short walkthroughs of how neural networks and backpropagation work.

byjhpzEoXFs.summary: Timothy Gowers thinks aloud, in real time, as he tries to understand why Pascal's determinant equals 1. He does not fully solve it in this episode, but shows his exploratory process.
byjhpzEoXFs.why: HN commenters recommend it to see how a top mathematician approaches an unfamiliar problem through experiments and curiosity.

b0EF0VTs9Dc.summary: Douglas Crockford's Google Tech Talk explains monads without category theory or Haskell, implementing them in JavaScript and tying them to Ajax and promises. He also touches on odd asides such as coloring code by scope.
b0EF0VTs9Dc.why: Often recommended as a demystifying monad talk in plain JavaScript, though some find it light on definitions.

b9FC9fAlfQE.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog shows hand soldering of surface-mount parts, including drag soldering and tack-and-reflow of 0.5mm fine-pitch ICs, with solder paste and hot air.
b9FC9fAlfQE.why: Recommended as a good introduction to SMD soldering techniques for beginners.

bAUVCn_jw5I.summary: Tim Dodd's hour-long deep dive on how rocket engines start, from solid motors to liquid engines. It covers thermal conditioning, spin-up, ignition methods, starting in space, and a step-by-step RS-25 startup.
bAUVCn_jw5I.why: HN recommends it as the best explanation of why engine start is hard and what can go wrong.

bL6hp8BKB24.summary: RocketJump Film School argues that we only notice bad CG while great CG is invisible, so CG seems to be everywhere ruining movies when it often is not.
bL6hp8BKB24.why: Used as a counterpoint whenever commenters claim CGI always looks fake.

bfN2JWifLCY.summary: UnHerd interview with Swedish epidemiologist Johan Giesecke, who explains why he thinks lockdowns are the wrong policy and describes Sweden's approach during the spring 2020 pandemic.
bfN2JWifLCY.why: Commenters point to it for the Swedish insider perspective on lockdowns, with some later calling its statements prescient.

boPEO2auJj4.summary: Timur Doumler's CppCon 2015 talk on how C++ is used in the audio industry. It covers the patterns and tools audio developers rely on, including handling real-time constraints.
boPEO2auJj4.why: HN commenters recommend it as an introduction to real-time and low-latency programming in C++ for people getting into audio.

bvim4rsNHkQ.summary: SpaceX's own compilation of failed orbital booster landing attempts, set to sound, showing the crashes before landings succeeded.
bvim4rsNHkQ.why: HN uses it as evidence that SpaceX iterated through visible failures and is open and humorous about them.

b9IkpUYlOx8.summary: Pianist Tom Brier sight-reads a piano arrangement of the Super Mario World ending theme, working from a first-draft score by Keeper1st. He takes some liberties with the score as he plays.
b9IkpUYlOx8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a showcase of remarkable sight-reading and a favorite when sight-reading or notation comes up.

bB340S0tGf8.summary: Kai Lentit's comedy sketch parodying an interview with an agile coach, lampooning scrum, sprints and kanban jargon. It is a few minutes of programmer humor.
bB340S0tGf8.why: Recommended as a funny parody that resembles agile as practiced at large companies.

bM0PmwOlifE.summary: Matthew Cole's Black Hat 2013 talk on operational security failures by CIA operatives. It covers the Abu Omar case and how sloppy tradecraft with cell phones exposed officers through call records and metadata.
bM0PmwOlifE.why: HN commenters cite it as a compelling demonstration that metadata identifies people, and as a great watch on sloppy CIA tradecraft.

baFaEvBywGc.summary: An episode of Tim Hunkin's The Secret Life of Machines that explains how a washing machine works, using models, cut-aways and animations. It was first aired in 1988.
baFaEvBywGc.why: Recommended as a humorous and clear explanation of everyday machines, including why washing machine balancing works.

bnoUBfLxZz0.summary: A Wendover Productions documentary-style video on how Zipline delivers blood and medical supplies by drone in Rwanda. It covers the catapult launch, parachute drop and the logistics behind it.
bnoUBfLxZz0.why: Offered as a clear, well-made look at a real, working drone-delivery system, often in answer to skepticism about delivery drones.

bwDrHqNZ9lo.summary: A one-minute clip of Slavoj Zizek showing what he calls the official geographical limit between the Balkans and Central Europe, standing at a river in Ljubljana. It is a short, absurd and funny piece of cultural geography.
bwDrHqNZ9lo.why: HN commenters recommend it as one of the best short clips on YouTube for illustrating Balkan versus Central European identity.

b1JlYZQG3lI.summary: Wendover Productions explains the wave of supply shortages in 2021, arguing the causes go beyond COVID. It covers how just-in-time manufacturing was applied, container imbalances and the chip shortage.
b1JlYZQG3lI.why: HN commenters point to it as a better explanation of just-in-time versus the Toyota Way and of container and chip shortages.

b1NTaVQPt1E.summary: Chris Seaton talks about JRuby+Truffle, explaining how the Truffle and Graal combination optimises the tricky parts of Ruby and why it outperforms other Ruby implementations.
b1NTaVQPt1E.why: HN recommends it for specifics on how Truffle and Graal achieve strong dynamic-language performance.

b5P3QDm61go.summary: Apple's 2002 television ad for the iMac G4 "Lamp", showing the adjustable-arm design in a playful way.
b5P3QDm61go.why: Cited in iMac G4 threads as a charming ad reminiscent of Pixar's Luxo Jr.

b9_Vh9h3Ohw.summary: The Verge's documentary on Handspring and its Treo, a smartphone that came a decade before the iPhone. It tells how a small team tried to build the modern smartphone and was held back by carriers and timing.
b9_Vh9h3Ohw.why: HN recommends it as an interview-rich history of Handspring, Palm OS and why telcos hurt early smartphones.

bHJyoqDO0zw.summary: An MIT colloquium by Dennis Whyte on power exhaust and first-wall cooling in fusion reactors, including recent innovations and the SPARC and ARC designs.
bHJyoqDO0zw.why: Recommended for realistic engineering detail on extracting heat from a tokamak.

bKgf5PaBzyg.summary: A bizarre, tongue-in-cheek video in which John McAfee himself supposedly shows how to uninstall McAfee antivirus. It is known for its NSFW sex and drug references.
bKgf5PaBzyg.why: HN mostly cites it as a notorious piece of McAfee lore, usually jokingly, whenever John McAfee or antivirus uninstallation comes up.

bLk1cjZ4ll0.summary: Technology Connections praises a 1940s-50s Sunbeam toaster and explains what makes a toaster well designed, drawing on a vintage Sunbeam video.
bLk1cjZ4ll0.why: Recommended as a passionate take on good appliance design and cited in toaster threads.

bPhUhypV27w.summary: A deepfake in which Bill Hader, impersonating Arnold Schwarzenegger on a talk show, visibly morphs into Schwarzenegger. It was made with DeepFaceLab by Ctrl Shift Face.
bPhUhypV27w.why: Pointed to as one of the most impressive early deepfakes, where a good impersonation makes the effect convincing and funny.

bl8jQ2wRh6k.summary: Elias Martenson presents his Emacs-based workflow for building a web application (the Potato chat platform) with Common Lisp on the backend and ClojureScript on the frontend. He demonstrates SLIME, Paredit, CIDER and debugger-driven interactive development. The talk is 79 minutes and was given at Emacs SG.
bl8jQ2wRh6k.why: HN commenters point to it as a live demonstration of interactive Lisp development, including compiling single functions in a running program and debugger-driven workflows.

bqPARIKHbN8.summary: VICE's Oobah Butler spends eight months using fake reviews to push a nonexistent restaurant, The Shed at Dulwich, to number one on TripAdvisor in London. The short documentary shows how easily review systems can be gamed.
bqPARIKHbN8.why: Cited as the canonical example of fake reviews and gamed rating platforms.

bzkRVzciAZg.summary: A short satirical sketch in which a Q&A about web servers turns into a profane rant about threads, blocking and non-blocking I/O. It lampoons the hype around Node.js and async programming.
bzkRVzciAZg.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke in async, Node and concurrency threads, and some call it hysterically funny.

bKH5nGLgi08.summary: A 36C3 talk on the AMD Platform Security Processor, an undocumented ARM core inside AMD CPUs that runs before the main processor. The speakers present their reverse engineering of its internals.
bKH5nGLgi08.why: Cited in discussions of open firmware and trust as a thorough reverse engineering of the PSP.

bX3EZCVj2XA.summary: A clip of a 1984 interview with KGB defector Yuri Bezmenov describing Soviet ideological subversion and demoralization of a target society, uploaded with a politically charged framing.
bX3EZCVj2XA.why: Mostly cited as a source for the demoralization and subversion idea, though one commenter dismisses it as alt-right material.

b1HWNcLDK88.summary: A full FRONTLINE interview with journalist Julia Ioffe on Putin and alleged Russian interference in the 2016 US election.
b1HWNcLDK88.why: Recommended for historically grounded analysis of Putin, and praised as an example of releasing full-length interviews.

b2mnbyRgXkY.summary: Day one of the X.Org Developer's Conference 2020 stream, including talks on the Raspberry Pi 4 Vulkan driver, the WSL graphics architecture, X11 and Wayland apps in WSL, and Mesa for D3D12.
b2mnbyRgXkY.why: Linked for the Microsoft talks on WSL GUI support and how WDDM drivers map into the Linux VM.

b6URa-PTqfA.summary: A 1979 BBC Nationwide report asking whether word processors and networked microprocessors could end office commuting. It shows early word processing and a woman working from home, with surprisingly prophetic predictions.
b6URa-PTqfA.why: HN finds it a striking historical look at early text editors and remote work that feels very modern.

b9ifQvQCO7Y.summary: A concept video from 2003 showing an early vision of Windows Longhorn's interface, before it shipped as Vista.
b9ifQvQCO7Y.why: Cited to contrast Microsoft's ambitious Longhorn vision with the Vista that actually shipped.

bBx2Y5HhplI.summary: Nick Hanauer's short TED University talk on economic inequality, which was famously not posted on TED's main site at first. He argues that rich people are not the job creators.
bBx2Y5HhplI.why: Cited in debates about taxes, job creation and wealth redistribution, and for the controversy around its release.

bEOOYbscyTs.summary: Dragan Djuric presents Clojure libraries for GPU and numerical computing, including ClojureCL, ClojureCUDA and Neanderthal. He shows how a dynamic REPL workflow can be combined with low-level hardware acceleration for machine learning and data science.
bEOOYbscyTs.why: HN commenters point to it as the talk by the author of Neanderthal and the Clojure GPU libraries, including comparisons against the JVM and CPU.

bJ_seXo-Enc.summary: Tom Scott tours the rotating room artificial gravity facility at Brandeis University's Graybiel lab. It shows how humans cope with rotation-based gravity and the odd effects such as Coriolis forces.
bJ_seXo-Enc.why: HN cites it as an intuitive demonstration of the Coriolis effect and the practical problems of spinning habitats.

bQECSInWVPY.summary: A one-minute clip of Steve Jobs at the D3 conference in 2005 discussing virtual reality. He compares VR headsets to headphones for video, an analogy later applied to Apple's Vision Pro.
bQECSInWVPY.why: HN commenters cite it in Vision Pro and AR threads as Jobs's concise take that a headset is like headphones for video.

bQfJi7rjuEk.summary: Bryan Cantrill's Monktoberfest 2023 talk takes on AI doomerism, weighing the theoretical existential risks against the reality on the ground. He takes a skeptical but thoughtful view of how to balance AI's potential against its risks.
bQfJi7rjuEk.why: Recommended as a thoughtful Cantrill talk on embracing failure and curiosity in engineering, and as a skeptical counterpoint to AI doom narratives.

bS5P_LAqiVg.summary: Kung Fury is a 30-minute crowd-funded 80s action comedy about a kung fu cop who travels back in time to kill Hitler, packed with retro tropes.
bS5P_LAqiVg.why: Cited as a parody that crams in 80s movie tropes and as an example of the VHS aesthetic.

b_T-eCToX1I.summary: Daniel Dunbar of Apple presents llbuild, a framework for building build systems, at the 2016 LLVM Developers' Meeting. He argues that the traditional way C compilers integrate with build systems limits compile speed, and proposes a new architecture.
b_T-eCToX1I.why: Cited in build-system and C++ compile-time threads as Apple's work on incremental builds and the design behind llbuild.

bdJKjBHCh18.summary: A short clip of Leo Laporte interviewing Bill Atkinson about developing HyperCard, including his story that the idea came during an LSD experience.
bdJKjBHCh18.why: HN links it as the source of the story that HyperCard was inspired by an acid trip.

bhyYgnhhKFw.summary: CGP Grey breaks down what the British Royal Family costs the UK versus what it brings in, including income from royal-owned land. He concludes the government nets a profit from the arrangement.
bhyYgnhhKFw.why: HN commenters cite it in monarchy debates as the explainer claiming the royals make money for the UK, with some disputing it.

bj8hMtWeTUg.summary: A one-month review of the Xreal (formerly Nreal) Air AR glasses by The Tech Chap, covering unboxing, setup, what the display looks like, and how mixed reality differs from AR. It ends with the reviewer's overall thoughts. The video is sponsored.
bj8hMtWeTUg.why: HN uses it as a concrete example of lightweight AR glasses that work as a monitor replacement, a more comfortable alternative to VR headsets.

boB6qu5dcCw.summary: Nature video showing MIT researchers flying the first plane with no moving parts, powered by an ion drive that creates an ionic wind from high-powered electrodes. The 5m-wide craft flies across a sports hall.
boB6qu5dcCw.why: Linked as a quick demonstration of the ion plane in threads about silent aircraft and flying cars.

bq2_wSsDwkQ.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on the decline of the newspaper industry and what it means for journalism, including local reporting. It uses John Oliver's comedic commentary and references the film Spotlight.
bq2_wSsDwkQ.why: HN cites it in discussions of news economics and repackaged reporting, though some commenters say they distrust Oliver as a source.

bvlzZnhZhrc.summary: CBC Marketplace investigates locksmith scams in the Greater Toronto Area. It exposes networks of fake Google Maps listings and fake reviews, and uses hidden cameras to show how low quotes turn into overcharges.
bvlzZnhZhrc.why: Cited as a concrete demonstration of how fake local business listings on Google Maps are used for scams.

bwhU9goCiaI.summary: Asianometry traces the 30-year rise and peak of Japan's semiconductor industry from the 1950s to the 1980s, covering how a postwar country gained competence in an emerging technology.
bwhU9goCiaI.why: HN points to it as an excellent history of how Japan entered chips, including government-coordinated cooperation like the VLSI project.

by1xpy8ob8E.summary: Scott Manley explains the Cold War experiments in which steel and aluminium spheres, known as Lew Allen's Balls, were placed near nuclear detonations. The spheres survived the fireball, and he walks through what the declassified results show.
by1xpy8ob8E.why: Cited as a fun, well-explained account of objects surviving nuclear blasts, relevant to Orion-style and spacecraft survivability discussions.

b0Ti-gkJiXc.summary: Jay Smooth's short video on how to tell someone their words sound racist. He argues for focusing on what the person said or did rather than labeling who they are.
b0Ti-gkJiXc.why: HN commenters cite it in arguments about criticism, to separate attacking a comment from attacking a person.

b1XGPvbWn0A.summary: A short viral video of a woman walking through New York City for ten hours while being filmed receiving street harassment. It was made to illustrate catcalling.
b1XGPvbWn0A.why: Cited in discussions of street harassment as an illustration of what women experience in public.

b2F-DItXtZs.summary: A satirical animated dialogue in which a naive developer insists MongoDB is web scale while a database expert mocks him. It parodies the NoSQL versus relational debate.
b2F-DItXtZs.why: Posted as a classic meme whenever MongoDB, NoSQL hype or tech fads come up.

b3dYS7PcAG4.summary: A short Louis CK stand-up bit about complaining on airplanes, about how people take the miracle of flight for granted.
b3dYS7PcAG4.why: Posted as a joke reply to complaints about air travel and airport security.

b5wfPlgKFh8.summary: A 1986 SNL sketch in which Phil Hartman's Reagan seems clueless in public but is a scheming mastermind in private.
b5wfPlgKFh8.why: Used mainly as a reference for how contemporaries viewed Reagan's presidency, and occasionally as a joke.

b9UO9tn4MpI.summary: Two experimenters hold blades of grass near a radio transmitter antenna and hear the AM station through the arc between antenna and grass. It is a short, informal demonstration of unintentional AM demodulation.
b9UO9tn4MpI.why: HN commenters bring it out whenever AM radio, strong transmitters or accidental demodulation comes up, as the classic example of grass playing radio.

b9j-sfP9GUU.summary: Highlights of the June 2010 ICANN DNSSEC root Key Signing Ceremony, showing the procedures used to generate and protect the root zone signing key.
b9j-sfP9GUU.why: HN cites it to show how seriously root key ceremonies are secured and to let people watch one.

b9yL5usLFgY.summary: A one-minute skateboarding clip with a wreck in which a helmet likely prevented serious injury. It shows downhill longboarding without brakes.
b9yL5usLFgY.why: Used as an example in helmet and longboarding safety discussions.

bAF35dekiAY.summary: A scene from the BBC's Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy TV series in which Arthur argues vegetarianism in a restaurant where the dish of the day cheerfully offers up parts of its own body.
bAF35dekiAY.why: Posted as a joke in threads about livestock, animal intelligence and ethics of eating meat.

bC6tngl0PTI.summary: Tom Scott explains why Windows does not let you name a file CON, tracing the reserved device names back to backwards compatibility with DOS.
bC6tngl0PTI.why: Linked as a relevant explainer in threads about Windows quirks and reserved names.

bErPsq5kPzE.summary: Epic Games shows how LED walls can provide both virtual backgrounds and real lighting, letting scenes be captured in camera in a single pass with Unreal Engine.
bErPsq5kPzE.why: Cited as an example of LED volume virtual production, as used for Star Wars shows, in threads about VFX.

bHLR3faI7lU.summary: A short clip from the film Grandma's Boy showing JP's cluttered, reclined office setup, with a song playing in the background. It is a comedic movie scene rather than an instructional video.
bHLR3faI7lU.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in desk setup and workspace threads, and as an example of an appealing reclined desk with eye-level monitors.

bMJaMy-0ChA.summary: Not Just Bikes explains Dutch bicycle-only roads, which let people travel long distances in and out of cities with almost no car interaction. It shows how this changes cycling from a chore into something enjoyable.
bMJaMy-0ChA.why: HN commenters use it as an example of segregated bike infrastructure and of how quiet and pleasant car-free streets are.

bNpx7gpSqbY.summary: Bill Gross, who has founded and incubated many start-ups, ranked hundreds of companies on five factors. He presents the one factor that stood out as the biggest predictor of success.
bNpx7gpSqbY.why: HN commenters cite it for its finding that timing is the most important factor in startup success.

bO4jHXjCXw8.summary: A short Channel NewsAsia interview clip in which MasterCard's Southeast Asia president voices distrust of cryptocurrencies produced by anonymous computers in anonymous places. It is part of the Perspectives series and runs about four minutes.
bO4jHXjCXw8.why: Cited, usually critically, as a window into how payment companies view cryptocurrency and cash.

bT3G-kcKN70.summary: An IIHS news release video showing crash tests in which truck underride guards fail at relatively low speeds. The institute petitions for a stronger federal standard.
bT3G-kcKN70.why: Cited in Tesla Autopilot crash threads to show how deadly car-into-trailer crashes are and why underride guards matter.

bU1QPtOZQZU.summary: A Discovery Channel computer simulation of a large asteroid impact on Earth, showing the scale of the devastation. It sits in a broader context of early Earth impacts and the moon-forming collision.
bU1QPtOZQZU.why: HN commenters link it to convey the scale of asteroid impacts, such as the one that killed the dinosaurs, or of ejecta and tsunamis.

bV9ppvY8Nx4.summary: LegalEagle analyzes Katko v. Briney, the Iowa case about a homeowner whose shotgun booby trap injured a burglar, and the limits on deadly force in defending property.
bV9ppvY8Nx4.why: HN cites it as a source on the illegality of lethal booby traps, including in discussions of trapping hackers.

bZe5J8SVCYQ.summary: A short clip of the famous Hitchhiker-style circular narration of a missile guidance system explaining how it knows where it is by knowing where it isn't. It is a deadpan bit of technical-sounding absurdity about subtraction and navigation.
bZe5J8SVCYQ.why: HN commenters post it as an obligatory joke reply whenever threads touch on missiles, GPS, or circular reasoning.

b_WmjWAGkLI.summary: Amateur footage from 2014 of small airplanes being lifted and blown around during a microburst. It is a three-minute clip showing how violent the gusts can be.
b_WmjWAGkLI.why: Linked as a vivid real-world illustration of wind gusts and lift acting on aircraft.

bct8stbZafI.summary: A short clip from Anthony Bourdain's Parts Unknown in which he and chef Sean Brock end a long night of drinking at a Charleston Waffle House. It celebrates the unpretentious, welcoming late-night diner. Bourdain's remark comparing the meal favorably to the French Laundry is what people remember.
bct8stbZafI.why: HN commenters cite it whenever Waffle House comes up, as a touchstone for Bourdain's love of humble, unfancy places.

bdwjcayPuag.summary: A one-minute Rheinmetall promotional demo of Oerlikon Ahead air burst ammunition, which throws a cloud of sub-projectiles to destroy small air targets.
bdwjcayPuag.why: HN cites it as an example of programmable airburst ammunition used against drones and fast aircraft.

bexWuHmV32A.summary: An over-the-shoulder view of StarCraft 2 pro player Sound at a WCS qualifier, showing his monitor, keyboard and mouse. It shows his very fast actions per minute in real time.
bexWuHmV32A.why: HN commenters cite it as an example of expert human multitasking and heavy keyboard use with sparing mouse use.

bg6-LVCHmGM.summary: A collection of lightning talks from the Surge 2015 conference on scalable systems, hosted by Geir Magnusson. HN mostly points to one segment, a Bryan Cantrill talk touching on madvise semantics.
bg6-LVCHmGM.why: Cited as a classic Cantrill talk when threads discuss madvise, malloc and Dirty COW behavior.

bhtO4DsSazc.summary: A performance recording of Alvin Lucier's 1969 experimental piece in which a spoken text is repeatedly played back and re-recorded in a room until the room's resonances overwhelm the words. It is a landmark of electronic and conceptual music.
bhtO4DsSazc.why: HN people cite it as a canonical example of iterative degradation and as an analogy for repeated copying, AI bot loops, and dissociative listening.

bsHryqnvyYA.summary: An ETH Zurich lab demonstration of a failsafe algorithm that lets a quadrocopter detect the loss of a propeller and recover, returning to its original position.
bsHryqnvyYA.why: HN cites it to show that a quadcopter can keep flying after losing a rotor, though under ideal lab conditions.

bt73GOk4JRY.summary: A promotional video from Oxbo showing its blueberry and raspberry harvesting machines in operation. It demonstrates mechanical berry harvesting at commercial scale.
bt73GOk4JRY.why: HN cites it as evidence that commercial berry harvesting is done by mechanical shaking and agitation, in contrast to slow picking robots.

buqtdpuZxvk.summary: The Galaxy Song from Monty Python's The Meaning of Life, a comic musical tour of the size and motion of the galaxy and our place in it.
buqtdpuZxvk.why: HN people drop it as a joke in threads about stars, galaxies, and cosmic scale.

bx_LGilOuE4.summary: Martin von Zweigbergk presents Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible VCS with undo, anonymous branches, first-class conflicts, automatic rebasing, and the working copy as a commit. He also covers plans at Google.
bx_LGilOuE4.why: HN links it as the canonical talk on Jujutsu's design, especially conflict handling.

bzE-IMaegzQ.summary: Casey Neistat's early viral short in which he gets ticketed for not using a bike lane in New York, then shows how often the lanes are blocked by cars and other obstacles. It runs about three minutes.
bzE-IMaegzQ.why: Referenced in bike-lane threads as the classic example of how NYC bike lanes get blocked and how cyclists get ticketed.
